dct_description_sm: Ice-rich landscapes across the Northwest Territories have the potential to undergo substantial modification in response to climate induced permafrost degradation. Thermokarst will pose an increasing risk to communities, infrastructure and northern ecosystems. It also poses risks to cultural landscapes. Cultural landscapes preserve a long-term record of the conduct of indigenous traditional practices (hunting, fishing, trapping, travelling, etc) on the land in the form of sacred sites, traditional trails, critical harvesting areas, archaeological sites, and other heritage sites. The objective of the project was to develop a vulnerability index tool for climate change-induced threats to community heritage resources in the Gwich'in Settlement Area. The project would help identify which community heritage sites are prone to disturbances such as retrogressive thaw slumps, and would help prioritize efforts to mitigate impacts to the most important sites.

dct_title_s: Terrain Mapping and Community Heritage Resource Management: Adapting to Climate Change in the Gwich'in Settlement Area
